cites.quote: One bookable interval of a doctor's slot length, starting at the start of an availability block.
A past slot with a non-cancelled appointment counts as booked; a past slot without one counts as neither.
Each row links to the doctor page with a `?date=` parameter set to that row's date (YYYY-MM-DD).
The rest of the doctor page is `unchanged`
then the 15 Nov row counts that slot as free, not booked, matching the day schedule for 15 Nov

findings.suggested_fix: List all the 15 Nov slots and state the expected counts, for example booked 0 and free 1, as S-1 AC2 does.
findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (F-2): S-1 AC4 lists no other 15 Nov slots and gives no expected booked/free numbers, so 'counts that slot as free' can only be checked by comparing with the day schedule.

cites.quote: Given an active doctor whose slots on 14 Nov are 09:00, 09:30 and 10:00 local
Given an active doctor with no availability block on the weekday of 16 Nov

findings.suggested_fix: Add a clock to each Given, for example 'the clock is 12 Nov 10:00 local'.
findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (F-3): S-1 AC2, S-1 AC4 and S-2 AC1 use 14, 15 and 16 Nov but fix no clock, so it is not set that those dates fall inside the 7-day window.

findings.suggested_fix: Split S-4 into one story for REQ-9 and one for REQ-10.
findings.text: Still open from attempt 1 (F-4): S-4 still combines two outcomes, no section for inactive doctors (REQ-9) and the rest of the page unchanged (REQ-10).

cites.quote: shows exactly what it shows today when 16 Nov is picked by hand

findings.suggested_fix: Say 'on the build before this change', as S-4 does.
findings.text: S-3 AC4 uses 'today' to mean 'in the current build'. Elsewhere 'today' means the local date, so a reader could take it as a date.

rubric_items.reason: S-1 to S-4 trace all ten known requirements, REQ-1 to REQ-10. The intent has no assumed requirements.
S-1 to S-3 each have one outcome. S-4 still combines two: no section for inactive doctors (REQ-9) and the rest of the page unchanged (REQ-10).

The ACs use Given/When/Then and catch the likely wrong builds: the UTC/IST midnight case, how past slots count, and 'Not available' vs free 0. S-1 AC4 still gives no expected counts, and several dated ACs fix no clock.
S-4 AC3 and AC4 no longer name unsourced UI text. All other values come from the intent, or are example data or derived inline, such as UTC+05:30 for the 00:30 IST instant.
The terms match the glossary and the intent, and the prose agrees with the frontmatter. S-3 AC4 uses 'today' to mean 'currently', while elsewhere 'today' means a date.
